correctness.rationale: Count 14 conic-line intersections and 21 line pairs to force six conic-containing and five line-only triples. The simple 2-regular 6-vertex graph excludes two triangles and forces C6, its complementary triples and Pascal line. Two independent pencils admit the displayed normalized coordinates. Exact substitution forces v=(u-1)/u and the unique conic Q_u. The Pascal line restricts Q_u to a binary form with discriminant 4u²(u²-u+1) while det(Q_u)=-u²(u²-u+1)/4, so tangency contradicts conic smoothness. The standalone checker verifies each algebraic identity. No finite experiment substitutes for the quantified proof.

value.rationale: The eliminated node-free extreme basket (0,1,11) is one natural numerical corner of the 2022 degree-nine conic-line classification question, not an arbitrary parameter choice. Its impossibility follows from a nontrivial structural mechanism: a forced C6 incidence graph, two alternating pencils and the equality Δ=-16 det(Q) for their Pascal line. This useful realizability obstruction applies without any freeness hypothesis, while leaving other baskets and broader classification open.
